stories.title: Son-in-law arranging mother-in-law's funeral pyre eaten by crocodile:Father-in-law said, 'Who would jump into river to give their life'
stories.summary: In Gonda, a son-in-law who was preparing his mother-in-law's funeral pyre was dragged into the river by a crocodile. On Wednesday afternoon around 12 o'clock, he was digging a pit for the pyre at the Saryu river ghat. After digging, the young man went to the river bank to wash his hands. As soon as he lifted water from the river, the crocodile attacked. The crocodile clamped the young man's head in its jaws, then quickly dragged him underwater. People standing at the ghat kept screaming and shouting. Out of fear, they could not muster the courage to save the young man. Police started searching for the young man with the help of local boatmen. SDM Tarbganj also reached the spot. But no trace of the young man was found. SDRF has been called from Lucknow. The young man had come from Noida to attend his mother-in-law's last rites. The incident is from Umri Begamganj police station area, 35 km away from the district headquarters. Read the entire incident Woman died of cancer Babulal Verma (70) lives in Deeha village. He does farming. His son Lalchandra has passed away. In the family, there was his daughter-in-law Urmila (50), who died on Tuesday due to cancer. 5 years ago, Urmila's daughter Rekha was married to Deepak (30) of Greater Noida. Deepak lived in Pari Chowk. Both have a daughter Nikki (4). Deepak worked in a private company. He had come to Gonda with his wife and daughter to attend his mother-in-law's last rites. On Wednesday, the last rites were to be performed near the banks of the Saryu river at Sanauli Mohammadpur Udaybhan Pahi. Around 12 noon, everyone reached the riverbank. Deepak started hammering a stake at the riverbank to prepare the pyre. Crocodile grabbed his head in its jaws dragged him away Local people had already warned Deepak that there are crocodiles in the river, be careful. He was hammering a stake. After this, he reached the river bank to wash his hands. Deepak was washing his hands, meanwhile a crocodile came out of the river. It caught Deepak's head in its jaws. Seeing this, people ran towards Deepak and raised an alarm, but by then the crocodile had dragged him into the water. An eyewitness said that as soon as the crocodile dragged him, I tried to catch him, but it took him away. When I tried, I also fell into the water. Another eyewitness Aman said that Deepak was standing right there digging a pit. He had already been warned that a crocodile lives there. Don't go towards that side. Despite this, he went near the water to wash his hands. As soon as he bent down to wash his hands, the crocodile caught his head in its jaws and dragged him inside. People immediately informed the police about the accident. With the help of local boatmen, everyone joined in the search for Deepak. Upon receiving the information, police from Umri Begumganj station immediately reached the spot. Other teams along with local divers were also called. SDM Tarbganj reached the incident site and took stock of the situation. However, no trace of Deepak has been found yet. Grandfather-in-law said- No one tried to save him Babu Lal said, our daughter-in-law had already died. I have no one before or after me. Relatives were preparing for the entire funeral rites. A post was being set up for the last rites, just then a crocodile came and dragged away my son-in-law. No one tried to save him, who would jump into the water to give their life? Lucknow SDRF Called Gonda's District Disaster expert Rajesh Srivastava informed that an SDRF team has been called from Lucknow for the rescue operation, but the team has not reached the spot yet. Meanwhile, local people along with the Revenue Department team were conducting a search operation using boats, but they did not achieve any success. After this, the search operation has been stopped. He informed that upon recovery of Deepak's body, financial assistance of Rs 4 lakh will be provided to the family members after post-mortem. If the body is not recovered, then a letter will be sent to the government seeking permission and necessary guidelines to provide financial assistance.

Here are the top news headlines of the day- 1. 15 lakh drug stores closed due to nationwide chemist strike More than 15 lakh medical stores across India will remain closed on Wednesday following a nationwide shutdown call by the All India Organisation of Chemists and Druggists (AIOCD). 2. Rahul Gandhi calls PM and HM ‘traitors': Says economic storm is coming Rahul Gandhi launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah during a public meeting in Raebareli. Addressing the Bahujan Swabhiman Sabha in Lodhwari village on Wednesday, Rahul Gandhi claimed that an “economic storm” was approaching and alleged that the Centre would not be able to protect the public. 3. Detergent used to make fake milk in UP: 20 litres converted into 80 within minutes Milk is often considered a rich source of calcium and an essential part of a balanced diet that supports overall well-being and boosts metabolism. But what if the milk you consume turns out to be synthetic and potentially harmful to your health? 4. Putin's China visit: Bilateral talks held in Beijing The Russian President Vladimir Putin was welcomed by the Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing after a military inspection on Wednesday. 5. Midnight power cuts in Lucknow frustrates residents, angered crowd storms power house Public anger over prolonged power cuts erupted across Lucknow on Tuesday, with angry residents staging protests in several areas. Hundreds of people stormed the RDSO power house in Kesri Khera ward late at night, forcing officials and employees to flee the spot. 6. Chirag Paswan planning to contest UP assembly polls alone Chirag Paswan’s party, Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) [LJP(R)], has decided to contest the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections after Bihar and Jharkhand. The party plans to field candidates on all 403 seats in UP and preparations have already begun. Large posters of Chirag Paswan are being put up across cities from Lucknow to Ayodhya. 7. WhatsApp, Facebook Instagram to fire 8,000 employees News agency ANI said on Wednesday, 20 May, 2026, that according to a report by NBC News, the owner of WhatsApp, Facebook Instagram will shift around 7,000 employees into AI-focused roles. 8. Akhilesh promises 69,000 jobs and caste census if voted to power SP chief Akhilesh Yadav held a press conference at the party office in Lucknow on Wednesday. Regarding the uproar over reservation in the 69,000 teacher recruitment, he said that they would complete the recruitment process within 90 days of coming to power. They will help the candidates. They will ensure justice for them. He also said that they would conduct a caste census as soon as they come into government. 9. UP govt plans to bring law against Chinese manjha The Allahabad High Court’s Lucknow Bench took a strict stance on the issue of Chinese manjha in Uttar Pradesh during a hearing on Tuesday. The UP government informed the court that it is drafting a new law to curb the manufacture, sale and use of dangerous kite strings. 10. Virat Kohli richest in IPL with ₹230 crore earnings Virat Kohli has become the highest-earning player in the IPL, the Royal Challengers Bengaluru talisman has earned ₹230 crore. This claim has been made in the latest report by Fanatic Sports and Hurun India.

stories.title: Wife woke him at 5 am, husband dies by suicide:Usually slept till 8; told brother-in-law, “Look after your sister”
stories.summary: In Hathras, a young man took his own life on Wednesday morning simply because his wife had woken him up early. He usually slept until 8 AM every day. His wife had woken him up at 5 AM, three hours earlier. An argument broke out between them over this matter. After the argument subsided, the wife made tea and gave it to him. The husband drank the tea and called his brother-in-law. He said - "I am leaving now, take care of your sister." After this, he went inside the room and locked the door. After some time, the sound of a gunshot was heard from the room. The wife raised an alarm and called the nearby people. When the door was broken open, there was a blood-soaked body on the bed and a pistol lying nearby. The incident occurred in the Sikandrarau police station area, about 25 kilometers from the district headquarters. See two pictures... Now read the case in detail... Lalu used to do farming Lalu (35), son of Nawab Singh, was living with his family in Rampur Battari village. He was supporting his family by doing farming. 7 years ago, Lalu got married to Asha Devi from Etorni village. At home, there is a 6-year-old son Aarav and a 1-year-old daughter Aarohi. His elder brother lives separately with his family. The elderly parents also live with the elder son. Son Aarav studies in a private school near Kishanpur village and used to go to school by tempo. On Wednesday morning around 5 o'clock, his wife woke up to send her son to school. She finished the household chores, then was going to the kitchen to cook food. The kitchen gate was tight and Asha couldn't open it. To get the gate opened, she woke up her husband Lalu. Lalu got angry at being woken up early. An argument started between the two and Lalu beat his wife. After this, the wife sent the child to school. Around 7 o'clock, she made tea for her husband. After drinking the tea, Lalu locked the room. Called brother-in-law before taking his life After some time, Lalu called his brother-in-law and said, "This is our last meeting, I am going now, take care of your sister." After this, the sound of a gunshot from a pistol was heard. His wife came running but the door was locked from inside. When she raised an alarm, people from the neighborhood gathered and informed the police. When the wife's family members arrived, the door was broken open and Lalu's body was found lying on the bed with a pistol lying nearby. Wife said- He beat me over a trivial matter, then took his life Wife Asha Devi is in a terrible state, crying inconsolably. She said that she had woken up her husband to open the kitchen door. I said, get up now, it's already morning. I couldn't open the kitchen gate. Over this matter, my husband woke up from deep sleep and started fighting with me. After the quarrel, he beat me. Even after that, I made tea in anger and gave it to him. He had drunk the tea. Then he called my younger brother Manu. As soon as he finished the tea, he disconnected the phone and shot himself with a pistol, placing it against his head. Kotwal Shivkumar said- Police are investigating the matter. The illegal pistol found at the scene has been seized and necessary legal action has been initiated. Based on the statement of the family members, a case will be registered and further action will be taken.

stories.title: Violence erupts over petrol in Gorakhpur:Man suffers head injury, desperate buyers queue with gallons, many shut pumps upset them
stories.summary: Petrol and diesel shortages triggered chaos across Gorakhpur on Wednesday, with several fuel stations shutting down and residents standing in long queues for hours under extreme heat. The worsening crisis even led to violence at one petrol pump, where a young man suffered a head injury during a scuffle over fuel. Fuel shortage cripples city movement The petrol pump near Kali Mandir in Mohaddipur remained shut since Wednesday morning, while long queues were seen at fuel stations in Dharamshala and Town Hall areas. Residents carrying gallons and bottles waited anxiously for diesel and petrol supplies as stocks rapidly dried up. People complained of moving from one fuel station to another throughout the city, only to find shutters down and supplies exhausted within hours. Clash erupts over fuel supply Tension escalated at the Bakshipur petrol pump where a fight broke out among customers waiting for fuel. A young man suffered a head injury and was seen bleeding during the altercation. Videos of the incident quickly spread across social media platforms. Himanshu Srivastava, who had arrived to buy petrol, said he had already visited seven petrol pumps in the scorching heat before finally reaching the Town Hall station. Diesel rationing deepens public frustration At the Bharat Petroleum pump in Dharamshala, long queues of trucks, bikes and cars stretched outside the station. Residents claimed they had been waiting for nearly two hours. Many said diesel was being supplied only up to Rs 500 per customer, creating additional hardship for families and businesses already struggling with rising expenses. Some residents said weddings and transport work had been badly affected. Premium fuel sale draws criticism At the Town Hall petrol pump, customers were informed through display boards that only “Speed Petrol” was available. Residents alleged they were being forced to buy the premium-grade fuel at higher prices because regular petrol stocks had run out. Raunak Singh, who had been waiting for over half an hour, accused fuel stations of exploiting public helplessness during the shortage. Supply crunch worsens across outskirts Residents claimed they travelled nearly 10 kilometres searching for fuel across Rapti Nagar, Basaratpur, Deoria Bypass and Nausad, but most stations remained closed. In Piprauli’s Khanimpur area, an Indian Oil petrol pump remained completely shut on Wednesday. Locals said the station was receiving only one fuel tanker in two days, with stocks getting exhausted within five to six hours.

stories.title: Delegates from 8 countries to perform Panchkoshi Parikrama:BHU will conduct survey first, Professor says, 'Yatra will get world-class recognition'
stories.summary: BHU has received an important international project from the European Union related to religious tourism and cultural heritage conservation. Under this project named "Sacred Travels for Growth: Higher Education and Sustainable Growth Through Religious Tourism", 16 institutions and representatives from 8 countries around the world will work together to research religious travels, their traditions and conservation. Project highlights the importance of of ancient religious travels The main objective of this project is to understand the importance of ancient religious travels around the world including India, preserve them and connect religious tourism with sustainable development. Particularly, preparations are being made to present the historic Panchkoshi Yatra of Kashi at the global level. Soon, this journey will be organized for tourists coming from abroad. Initiative to Learn from Foreign Religious Journeys Professor Praveen Rana, associated with the project, said that he recently got an opportunity to visit Spain and Malta, where he closely observed and experienced the religious journeys and pilgrimage traditions there. He mentioned that European countries have preserved their religious journeys in a very organized manner. Taking inspiration from there, the Panchkoshi Yatra of Kashi is now being made a part of international research and cultural dialogue. He said that after returning to India, it was realized that Kashi's Panchkoshi Yatra also has the potential to gain global recognition. This year, due to Malmas (inauspicious month), a large number of devotees and tourists are arriving in Kashi, making this the right time to conduct an in-depth study of the challenges and possibilities of this pilgrimage. Detailed Survey to be Conducted on Panchkoshi Yatra BHU is now going to conduct a comprehensive survey on the Panchkoshi Yatra along with its students. Under this research, a study will be conducted on what is the cultural and social significance of religious sites, and what problems devotees face along the pilgrimage route. What steps can be taken to better develop and preserve this religious tradition? The research will also include topics such as travel route arrangements, facilities, cleanliness, security, cultural heritage, and participation of local people. After this, the complete report will be shared with the administration and research institutions so that it can be used in future planning. Representatives from 8 countries will undertake the Panchkoshi Yatra Professor Rana informed that foreign partners and researchers associated with the project are also being invited to Kashi. There is a plan for approximately 24 to 25 foreign delegates to come to Kashi and undertake the Panchkoshi Yatra. These delegates will not only be shown the ghats and lanes of Kashi. But they will also be introduced to the spiritual, cultural and historical tradition of the Panchkoshi Yatra. The objective of this initiative is that research institutions from around the world understand the religious journeys of Kashi and Indian traditions receive a new identity on the global platform. Now let us know what is the significance of Kashi's Panchkoshi Yatra The Panchkoshi Yatra is one of the most ancient sacred circumambulations of Kashi. This journey is of 25 kos, which is approximately 88 kilometers, which devotees undertake on foot. The Panchkoshi Yatra has five stops and this journey is of 5 days. This journey also has a direct connection with the Mahabharata period. This is where the journey begins This journey begins from Manikarnika Kund. Here devotees take a vow and start this journey. The first stop of this journey is Karmdeshwar Mahadev. After this, devotees stay in Shivpur on the second day. The third stop is Rameshwaram, the fourth is Bhimchandi and the last stop is Kapildhara. After that, devotees reach Manikarnika Kund and complete their journey. Moksha is attained According to religious beliefs, walking on this pilgrimage based on the boundaries of Kashi liberates devotees from the sins of birth and death, and a person directly attains Shiva Loka, meaning moksha (salvation). According to legends, the Pandavas also undertook this journey with the desire to regain their kingdom from Duryodhana. It was through the effect of this very journey that they got their kingdom back. Therefore, devotees undertake this sacred pilgrimage with the desire to fulfill their wishes.

stories.title: Massive fire breaks out at Ghaziabad chemical factory:Thick smoke visible from 3 km away; 12 fire tenders deployed
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out at a chemical manufacturing factory in Ghaziabad on Wednesday. This caused panic among the employees working in the factory. Upon receiving information, fire brigade teams reached the spot. The smoke rising from the fire is visible up to about 3 km away. People passing by the flyover also made videos of the incident. However, the cause of the fire has not yet been ascertained. Chief Fire Officer Rahul Pal informed that 12 fire engines have been called from Kotwali fire station and other stations to extinguish the fire. Fire personnel are engaged in bringing the fire under control. The matter is from the Kavinagar area of Vivekanand police station jurisdiction. Chief Fire Officer Rahul Pal said the fire department received information at 4:02 pm about a blaze at a chemical factory in Bulandshahr Industrial Area. Soon after the alert, five fire tenders from Ghantaghar Kotwali were rushed to the spot. Seven more fire engines were later called in from Vaishali, Modinagar and Noida. Water browsers and foam tankers were also used to douse the flames. The fire was brought under control within nearly an hour, though cooling operations are still underway. The cause of the blaze is being investigated, with a short circuit suspected to have triggered the fire. No casualties were reported in the incident.

stories.title: Police arrests groom on day of Nikah:Girl accuses man of rape in Deoria; says, 'Had affair for 7 years'
stories.summary: Wedding preparations were underway at home. The groom was getting ready. The wedding procession was about to leave in just a while. Just then, the police arrived and arrested the groom on charges of rape. The police say that a girl has accused the young man of sexual exploitation by giving false promises of marriage. He was arrested after registering a case based on her complaint. The girl alleges that the young man had an affair with her for 7 years. He established physical relations multiple times by giving false promises of marriage. Later, he backed out from his promise to marry. Now he is going to marry another girl. The case is from Deoria district. Now read the complete case... The incident is from a village in the Khukhundu police station area, 28 kilometers away from the district headquarters. Zeeshan Khan (28), who lives here, works as a carpenter in Saudi Arabia. Zeeshan's wedding was scheduled for May 19. The wedding procession was to go to Rani Patti in Bihar. Zeeshan had come to the village on leave on May 13. Family members said that on Tuesday afternoon, preparations for the wedding procession were underway at home. Just then, the police arrived and arrested Zeeshan and took him with them. When asked, the police said that a 25-year-old girl from the same village has filed a case against Zeeshan for rape by promising marriage. Girl said - He remained in constant contact over phone even from abroad The girl claims that Zeeshan had gone to Saudi Arabia for work about 2 years ago. During this time too, he kept talking continuously over the phone. He kept assuring her of marriage. Found out about the marriage when he returned from abroad The girl said - The family had fixed Zeeshan's marriage with another girl. But Zeeshan kept this matter hidden from me. On May 13, when Zeeshan returned to the village, I tried to meet him. But Zeeshan refused. That's when I came to know about his marriage being fixed. The accused is the middle of three brothers Villagers said that Zeeshan is the middle one among 3 brothers. His father does farming. The elder brother also lives abroad. Meanwhile, the girl who made the allegations has completed her graduation studies. Officer-in-charge JP Singh informed that the youth was arrested on rape charges and presented in court. From there, he has been sent to jail. The girl's medical examination has been conducted. The case is being investigated.

stories.title: Helicopter returning from Badrinath makes emergency landing in Tehri:Mid-air malfunction causes panic; hits electric wire while descending
stories.summary: A helicopter returning from Badrinath Dham with devotees from Delhi had to make an emergency landing in Tehri Garhwal on Wednesday morning. The helicopter suddenly developed a technical malfunction which caused it to become unbalanced in the air. As the situation worsened, the female pilot decided to land the helicopter in the fields below, but during landing, the rear part of the helicopter collided with an 11,000-volt power line. After the collision, the rear part of the helicopter was slightly damaged. Despite this, the female pilot showed presence of mind and safely landed the helicopter in a field located in Navgaon in the Satyo-Saklana area. All 7 people on board the helicopter, including the pilot, are safe. All passengers are said to be from the same family, residents of Punjabi Bagh in Delhi. The incident occurred on Wednesday morning at around 8:45 AM. As soon as the emergency landing happened, there was chaos in the area. Villagers from nearby areas rushed to the spot. After receiving information, police and administration teams also reached the scene and safely evacuated all passengers. See PHOTOS- Additional District Magistrate (ADM) Shailendra Singh Negi informed that the Trans Bharat Aviation Company's helicopter was going from Badrinath Dham to Guptkashi with 6 passengers. From there it had to proceed further to Dehradun. During this time, due to VIP movement in Guptkashi, the pilot was instructed to go directly to Dehradun. After changing the route, the helicopter reached above the Chamba-Arakot area. During this time, it came to light that there was a technical problem. According to the passengers and pilot, the helicopter started becoming unbalanced in the air and began descending. Collided with electric wire while attempting to land in a field When the situation became critical, female pilot Anupama Chaudhary decided to land the helicopter in the fields visible below. It was reported that while descending, the rear part of the helicopter came into contact with an 11000 volt high-tension electric wire. During this time, an electric wire got entangled in the rear part and rotor of the helicopter. The electric wire remained stuck in the helicopter from the Chamba-Arakot area to the landing site. This damaged the rear part of the helicopter. However, despite the critical situation, the pilot maintained the helicopter's balance and safely landed it in a field at Navgaon in the Satyo-Saklana area. Villagers gathered at the spot after emergency landing As soon as the helicopter made the emergency landing, people from nearby villages started reaching towards the fields. A crowd of villagers gathered at the spot. Local people also helped in evacuating the passengers. After receiving information, police and administration teams also reached the spot. Officials secured the entire area and movement of people around the helicopter was restricted. Female pilot is a resident of Meerut According to the ADM, the helicopter pilot Anupama Chaudhary is a resident of Meerut. Passengers also stated that during the critical situation, the pilot continuously tried to control the helicopter. Her presence of mind and quick decision averted a major accident. Investigation into incident begins, demand for technical inspection of helicopters Dhanolti Tehsildar Mohammad Shadab said that a detailed investigation into the causes of the incident is underway. Meanwhile, former district panchayat member and Congress leader Akhilesh Uniyal expressed concern over the incident, saying that people working in the field could also have been harmed by this. He has demanded strict technical inspection of all helicopters flying in the Chardham Yatra, so that such incidents can be prevented in the future.

stories.title: Akhilesh promises 69,000 jobs, caste census if voted to power:Shivpal Yadav attacks PM; says, 'He is misleading public'
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav held a press conference at the party office in Lucknow on Wednesday. Regarding the uproar over reservation in the 69,000 teacher recruitment, he said that they would complete the recruitment process within 90 days of coming to power. They will help the candidates. They will ensure justice for them. He also said that they would conduct a caste census as soon as they come into government. Actually, in 2019, the UP Basic Education Council conducted the examination for the recruitment of 69,000 assistant teachers. In the recruitment, there were a total of 18,598 seats in the OBC category, but OBC candidates were given only 2,637 seats. It is alleged that the Basic Education Rule 1981 and Reservation Rule 1994 have been violated in this recruitment. Seats reserved for the reserved category have been given to others. The High Court had also raised questions about the method of implementing reservation in the process. Akhilesh said that OBCs were given only 3.86% reservation instead of 27%. Similarly, SC candidates received only 16.6% reservation instead of 21%. This means there was a scam of 30%, or 20 thousand seats, with the PDA category. The most shameful thing is that 1133 posts for ST were left vacant. In the press conference, Shivpal Singh said - Where is the country's economy headed? How BJP people tell lies and only lies morning and evening. PM or CM, they are working to fool the public. Key points from Akhilesh's press conference- 1. The government is biased; whoever is biased is also treacherous Akhilesh presented the PDA audit report. His research team prepared it. He said, "If the youth have to knock on the court's door, then it should be understood that the government is biased. Whoever is biased is also treacherous. Bias is injustice. It suppresses rights and entitlements. Reservation is the only protector. Reservation is both a measure and a tool for equality." 2. Use bulldozers to give everyone equal rights The SP chief said- If the BJP government has to use bulldozers, then it should do so to level the uneven land of inequality. Give everyone equal rights. Now the question is, what is the real reason for rejecting reservation? In fact, for the last 5000 years, there have been two major divisions in society. On one side have been the dominant people, and on the other side, the deprived people. Their ratio has been 5% versus 95%. Babasaheb had endured this discrimination and suffering. Therefore, to eliminate centuries-old social discrimination, the provision of reservation was made in the Constitution, which continued smoothly until 2014. 3. The conspiracy to abolish reservation is becoming vocal After 2014, when a government of bias, deceit, and rhetoric came, those who used to remain underground started coming overground. The conspiracy to abolish reservation started becoming vocal. The thing is that BJP is that umpire who wants to win this battle of inequality that has been going on for centuries. They are being dishonest even in rules and decisions. Their attempt is to manage the court-like third umpire. BJP wants to shatter that ladder of reservation, with the help of which the deprived want to climb up. Only through reservation can democracy be saved. 4. I will not reveal any strategy for victory On the statement regarding reservation for Muslim women, Akhilesh said that our first job is to ensure rights and entitlements according to the population. We had also questioned the government on the Women's Reservation Bill, but they did not respond. On the question of vote rigging, he said- I will not reveal any strategy for victory. Otherwise, you will go and tell the BJP. 5. The government is neither allowing to earn nor to spend The SP chief said - The Chief Minister has nothing to do with the dollar. Let the dollar go anywhere. He has just been made to memorize that it's a 1 trillion dollar economy. Our country's economy is going down. The economy of a country is good where people spend more. PDA and Samajwadi Party are bringing down BJP's graph Akhilesh said - BJP people do not even discuss the 2024 elections. PDA and Samajwadi Party are bringing down BJP's graph. The graph of Samajwadi Party and PDA people is continuously going up. In the 2019, 2022, and 2024 elections, SP's graph has increased. BJP's is continuously going down. stories.title: Rahul warns of 'economic storm', calls PM, Amit Shah ‘traitors':Says, 'Modi will cry like he did during Covid and say it's not my fault'
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah during a public meeting in Raebareli. Addressing the Bahujan Swabhiman Sabha in Lodhwari village on Wednesday, Rahul Gandhi claimed that an “economic storm” was approaching and alleged that the Centre would not be able to protect the public. He said, “An economic storm is about to come. Narendra Modi and the Government of India will not be able to save you. Like during the Covid period, they will come before you crying and say it was not their fault.” ‘Mistake belongs to Modi, Shah and RSS’ Rahul Gandhi alleged that the Constitution had been weakened by the BJP leadership and the RSS. “I am telling you, the mistake belongs only to Narendra Modi, Amit Shah and the RSS because they have destroyed this,” he said while referring to the Constitution. He further said - When RSS workers approached you all, then yout should openly tell them that, your Prime Minister is a traitor, your Home Minister is a traitor, your organisation is a traitor. You have worked to sell India. ‘Respecting Veera Pasi and Ambedkar’s ideology is our responsibility’ Rahul Gandhi said that merely paying tribute to leaders such as Veera Pasi and B. R. Ambedkar was not enough, and their ideology must also be respected. He said, “If we fold our hands before Veera Pasi and Ambedkar, then it becomes our responsibility to honour their ideology.” Rahul added that if Ambedkar himself were present and people raised slogans in his support but later sided with forces opposing his ideology, it would amount to an attack on Ambedkar’s principles. See Photos- ‘RSS tears up Constitution in front of you’ Continuing his criticism of the RSS, Rahul Gandhi said people remained silent even when, according to him, the Constitution was being insulted. He said, “When RSS people tear up the Constitution in front of you, you remain silent. It is your blood and it is your responsibility to protect it.” Rahul raises issue of fuel and essential commodity prices Rahul Gandhi also spoke about inflation and rising fuel prices during his speech. He claimed that prices of petrol, diesel, cooking gas and food grains would rise sharply in the coming months. “Watch what happens to the prices of petrol, diesel, gas and pulses in the next few months,” he said. Allegations regarding Ambani and fuel exports Rahul Gandhi alleged that industrialist Mukesh Ambani was exporting fuel out of India while domestic fuel prices were rising. He claimed Ambani was buying fuel from Russia and selling it abroad, and further alleged that the profits were being used to fund Narendra Modi politically.

The party plans to field candidates on all 403 seats in UP and preparations have already begun. Large posters of Chirag Paswan are being put up across cities from Lucknow to Ayodhya. The posters carry slogans such as: “Why ask for support when our leader is ready?” and “UP First, UP people first.” The party leadership, including Chirag Paswan, has already announced that LJP(R) will contest the UP elections. Alliance with BJP limited to Bihar and Jharkhand Speaking to Bhaskar, LJP(R) MP and senior party leader Arun Bharti said the party’s immediate focus was on expanding its organisation in Uttar Pradesh. Bharti, who is also the MP from Jamui and Chirag Paswan’s brother-in-law, said the party was preparing to contest all seats in the state. On the possibility of an alliance, he said the party’s alliance with Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) existed only in Bihar and Jharkhand. “In UP, we currently have no alliance with any party. Neither have we formed one nor do we intend to,” he said. Organisation being strengthened from district to booth level With around eight months left before the Assembly elections, the party has started groundwork in the state. Arun Bharti said LJP(R) was focusing on strengthening the organisation from district to booth level. He said public opinion was also being sought regarding potential candidates in constituencies where the party already had a presence. Plan to project Chirag as North India leader Party leaders said the long-term goal was to establish Chirag Paswan as a major political face across North India. According to leaders, the party already has a strong presence in Bihar and has also contested elections in Jharkhand. Now, it plans to expand into Uttar Pradesh. They said Chirag Paswan had popularity across regions and the party had a support base in UP in the past, though it had not contested elections there in recent years. Focus on Purvanchal and Central UP According to party sources, LJP(R) plans to focus strongly on Purvanchal and Central Uttar Pradesh, where the Pasi community has a sizeable presence. Sources said the party had already conducted a preliminary-level survey and senior leaders were currently studying the data with experts. A senior party leader said some potential candidate names had also emerged during the first phase of the survey, though no official announcement would be made before a detailed review. Why Purvanchal and Central UP matter ? Party strategists believe Purvanchal and Central UP are politically significant for two key reasons. Firstly, districts in Purvanchal share a border with Bihar, meaning Bihar’s political influence is visible there. Secondly, around 3% of Uttar Pradesh’s population belongs to the Pasi community, which forms a major section of the state’s Dalit population. The community has significant influence in Central UP and Purvanchal. Party leaders believe the Paswan community of Bihar and the Pasi community of UP share social and political similarities. LJP(R) hopes to consolidate support among these groups. Leaders also feel the party has little to lose and much to gain politically in UP. Events planned around Pasi icons According to senior leaders, after the survey study is complete, the party will strengthen its organisational structure in all districts. It also plans to organise conferences of prominent Pasi leaders and events around icons from the Pasi community. Arun Bharti said party founder Ram Vilas Paswan had envisioned a Paswan-Pasi political alliance. Under this strategy, the party plans to hold birth anniversary events and conferences in the names of major Pasi figures across Uttar Pradesh. He said announcements regarding these programmes would be made soon. Attempt to occupy Dalit political space after Mayawati? Political analyst K.K. Lal said Chirag Paswan was a young leader with a long political future ahead. He said Ram Vilas Paswan had enjoyed strong influence in Bihar politics and was recognised as a national-level Dalit leader. According to Lal, Mayawati’s political influence has weakened with time and there is currently no strong pan-Hindi-belt Dalit face after her. He said Chirag Paswan appeared to be trying to occupy that political space. Could Chirag indirectly help BJP? Political observers also believe BJP may benefit indirectly if LJP(R) contests independently in UP. Analysts say BJP fears a shift of Dalit votes towards Bahujan Samaj Party or the SP-Congress alliance, especially after the 2024 Lok Sabha election results. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections- The INDIA bloc eventually won 43 of Uttar Pradesh’s 80 Lok Sabha seats. Earlier Bihar-based parties failed in UP This is not the first attempt by a Bihar-based party to expand into Uttar Pradesh. Earlier, Janata Dal (United) had also contested elections in UP. In the last Assembly elections, Mukesh Sahani’s party, Vikassheel Insaan Party (VIP), contested 105 seats independently in UP despite being part of the NDA alliance in Bihar. The party focused heavily on Purvanchal seats but failed to win a single seat. After the UP elections, BJP later merged VIP’s three Bihar MLAs into its own party. Mukesh Sahani was also removed from his ministerial post after the alliance collapsed. Meanwhile, JD(U) contested 16 seats in UP and managed to win two.

stories.title: Medical stores shut across UP today:Chemists protest against online sales; emergency medicines to remain available
stories.summary: Medical stores will remain closed in Lucknow and several other major cities of Uttar Pradesh on Wednesday, causing inconvenience to people trying to buy medicines. Shops in key medicine markets, including Aminabad, Charbagh and Chowk, remained shut from the morning as chemists joined a protest against online medicine sales. Traders alleged that e-pharmacy platforms were selling medicines without proper checks and pharmacist supervision, posing a risk to patient safety. According to chemist organisations, online medicine sales through fake prescriptions and heavy discounting are also affecting traditional medical businesses. In protest, traders across the state supported the shutdown. Traders protest against online sale of medicines The All India Organisation of Chemists and Druggists (AIOCD) had announced a 24-hour nationwide strike on May 20 against online medicine sales and heavy discounting by e-pharmacy companies. In Lucknow, traders protested under the banners of the AIOCD and the Lucknow Chemist Welfare Association. They alleged that online platforms were selling medicines without adequate verification and pharmacist supervision, which could prove dangerous for patients. ‘No compromise with patient safety’ Association president Amit Tiwari said the issue was not merely about business competition but directly linked to patient safety. He alleged that medicines were being sold using fake prescriptions, increasing the risk of incorrect treatment and harmful side effects. Concern over easy access to addictive drugs Drug traders also expressed concern that sleeping pills, painkillers and other restricted medicines were easily reaching young people through online platforms. According to traders, this could lead to a rise in drug abuse cases. Concerns over discounts and medicine quality Chemist organisations said online companies were offering medicines at heavy discounts, allegedly violating prescribed margin rules. They also raised concerns about counterfeit medicines and possible disruptions in the medicine supply chain. Despite the shutdown, trader organisations claimed that arrangements had been made to ensure the availability of emergency and life-saving medicines. Special arrangements were reportedly made at some places to ensure critically ill patients did not face major difficulties. Main demands of chemist organisations Chemist bodies have demanded that the government introduce stricter rules for online medicine sales, stop the use of fake prescriptions and make pharmacist supervision mandatory. They warned that if their demands were not met, the protest movement would be intensified further.

stories.title: Heatwave grips Uttar Pradesh:Banda records season’s hottest day at 48.2°C; schools shut and no relief expected for 10 days
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh has been reeling under severe heat for the past four to five days. On Tuesday, Banda recorded 48.2°C for the first time this season, making it the hottest city in the country and the third hottest in the world. Banda had earlier recorded 49.2°C in 2022. Weather officials say the four-year-old record could be broken in the coming days. Strong sunshine has been reported across most districts since Wednesday morning. Hot winds and rising humidity have made conditions extremely uncomfortable for residents. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a heatwave alert for 53 districts in the state. Hot winds from Balochistan and Thar desert worsening conditions According to the IMD, dry and extremely hot winds from Pakistan’s Balochistan region and the Thar desert are directly affecting the plains of north India. As a result, weather conditions usually seen in late May or June are already being experienced. The department has predicted intense heat across Uttar Pradesh for at least the next 10 days. Most districts are expected to remain under heatwave conditions, with daytime temperatures likely to range between 45°C and 49°C. People have been advised to avoid going outdoors between 12 noon and 4 pm. Schools shut in several districts due to heatwave Amid the severe heat, schools in several districts have been closed. In Mathura, all schools have been shut from May 20 until the start of summer holidays. Camps and special school events have also been banned. Summer vacations have also been declared in Ambedkar Nagar. In Varanasi, schools up to Class 12 have been closed till May 25. In Kanpur, Agra and Banda, schools up to Class 8 have been shut. Temple authorities issue advisories The management of Kashi Vishwanath Temple in Varanasi has advised devotees to avoid visiting during afternoon hours due to the extreme heat. At Banke Bihari Temple in Vrindavan, water is being sprinkled on mats laid on the temple platform to keep them cool for devotees. iPhones overheat in Lucknow, protests over power cuts The heat in Lucknow became so intense that iPhones reportedly began showing overheating alerts. Power cuts in several areas also triggered protests by residents late at night. Senior meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said weather conditions would remain clear across the state and temperatures in most districts would stay between 45°C and 49°C. He said there was no immediate possibility of relief from the heatwave. According to him, weather conditions may begin to change after May 29 due to the activation of a new western disturbance. He also said the monsoon could reach Kerala around May 26 and may enter Uttar Pradesh through Gorakhpur around June 18, although the date remains tentative. Weather forecast for next five days

stories.title: Midnight unrest over power cuts in Lucknow:Angry residents storm power house, officials flee amid protests; police rushed in from two stations
stories.summary: Public anger over prolonged power cuts erupted across Lucknow on Tuesday, with angry residents staging protests in several areas. Hundreds of people stormed the RDSO power house in Kesri Khera ward late at night, forcing officials and employees to flee the spot. Police teams from two police stations later reached the area after receiving information about the unrest. Similar protests were also reported at Ambedkar Power House in Nadarganj and in Rajajipuram’s Saripur area, where residents came out onto the streets over electricity outages. See 4 pictures- Trouble for population of 25,000 in Kesri Khera Local councillor Devendra Singh Yadav Jeetu said the transformer in Surya Nagar frequently breaks down. According to him, electricity department staff repair it during the day, but power supply fails again at night. He said around 25,000 residents were being affected by the recurring outages. On Tuesday night, nearly 1,000 angry residents surrounded the power house and raised slogans against the electricity department. Residents alleged that officials were not even answering phone calls, worsening the situation further. According to locals, the power supply went off around 7 pm and people continued protesting outside the power house late into the night. SSO flees during protest at Nadarganj Residents also staged a strong protest at Ambedkar Power House in Nadarganj over repeated power cuts. Protesters said they were fed up with daily outages and claimed that no official was listening to their complaints. Amid the protest, the SSO and other officials allegedly fled the power house. Strong protest in Kakori over four-day power crisis Residents of Janata Vihar Colony in the Kakori police station area said they had been facing a severe electricity crisis for the past four days. According to residents, the colony has been receiving electricity for only two to three hours a day. People complained of both low-voltage and high-voltage issues. The ongoing heatwave has also worsened the water shortage in the area. Angry consumers reached the FCI power house around 8 pm on Tuesday and staged a protest outside. The gate of the power house remained shut and no electricity department employee came out to address the complaints. The protest continued for nearly two hours. Residents Amit Kumar, Ramesh Rajput, Shivam Gautam, Aditya Kashyap and Rohit Gupta, among others, said the colony had only one transformer and there were also problems with damaged wires. In Dwarkapuri and Adarsh Vihar, they said, half the colony had electricity while the remaining areas remained in darkness. Kakori police reached the spot and tried to contact electricity department officials. Police assured residents that the supply would be restored by late night. Massive fire breaks out in electricity pole A major fire broke out in an electricity pole near Trikoneshwar Temple Bandha in Triveni Nagar-3, triggering panic in the area. Residents alleged that the incident was immediately reported to the electricity department, but officials did not answer calls. Locals warned that such negligence could lead to a major accident at any time. Panic spread among residents present near the site during the fire. Citizens demanded immediate action from the administration. Protest in Rajajipuram over prolonged outages Residents also protested in Rajajipuram over continuous power cuts. A resident named Utkarsh said he went to complain at Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited’s Rajajipuram C Block office regarding outages in Sector 12, Sector A and nearby areas. He said electricity supply had remained erratic for several days. Whenever complaints were lodged, officials allegedly responded that there was no lineman available and repairs would take time. According to him, power went out at 7 pm and had still not returned by 11 pm. Transformer catches fire in Faizullaganj Late at night, a transformer caught fire in Faizullaganj, disrupting electricity supply to nearby homes. Residents said they contacted electricity department officials, but no immediate solution was provided. Locals alleged that officials from LESA were informed immediately. When the junior engineer did not answer calls, residents contacted the SDO. They further claimed that the situation later led to an argument between two groups of local residents. Residents in Saripur take to streets People troubled by power cuts in Saripur area of Rajajipuram also came out onto the streets in protest. Residents said that when they reached the sub-station to lodge complaints, staff informed them that no lineman was available and the fault could not be repaired immediately. One resident said his wife was pregnant and the prolonged outage had created severe difficulties for the family.

stories.title: UP govt plans to bring law against Chinese manjha:Victims to get compensation; CM Yogi says, 'Murder case will be filed'
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court’s Lucknow Bench took a strict stance on the issue of Chinese manjha in Uttar Pradesh during a hearing on Tuesday. The UP government informed the court that it is drafting a new law to curb the manufacture, sale and use of dangerous kite strings. The proposed legislation may be named the Uttar Pradesh Deadly Manjha (Manufacturing, Sale and Use Prohibition) Act. The government also told the court that compensation would be provided to people affected by Chinese manjha incidents. The division bench of Justice Rajan Roy and Justice Manjeev Shukla said the matter was directly linked to the right to life and stressed that mere paperwork would not be enough, visible action on the ground was necessary. The next hearing has been scheduled for July 13, 2026. Strict ban planned on Chinese and glass-coated manjha The state government said the proposed law aims to impose a strict ban on Chinese manjha and glass-coated kite strings. At present, the proposal is in the drafting and deliberation stage. The sale of Chinese kite string is already completely banned in Uttar Pradesh, but authorities admitted that it continues to be sold illegally. The court was informed that while traditional Indian kite strings are made from normal thread, Chinese manjha is manufactured using nylon mixed with metallic, glass and iron powder to make it sharper and stronger. Due to the nylon material, the string does not snap easily during kite fights and is sharp enough to slit throats. Regarding deaths linked to Chinese manjha, UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had said on February 5 that murder charges would now be filed in such cases. Home Department issues fresh order, DGP circulates instructions The government informed the court that the Home Department issued a fresh government order on February 9, 2026, regarding action against Chinese manjha. Following this, the Director General of Police issued a circular on February 10 directing strict enforcement measures. A high-level committee was also formed on April 17 to monitor the issue. The government said multiple departments, including State Tax, Industrial Development, Home and Environment, were involved in tackling the problem. Amendments to the Police Act are also under consideration and a special enforcement campaign was recently launched. PIL filed in 2018 The matter stems from a public interest litigation filed in 2018 by Motilal Yadav and Rajjan Khan seeking a ban on Chinese manjha. After hearing the state government’s submissions, the High Court directed authorities to speed up deliberations on the proposed law and take concrete steps before the next hearing. The court observed that continuous and regular efforts were needed to stop the illegal and dangerous trade and stressed the importance of spreading awareness about the harmful effects of Chinese manjha. Traders allege harassment during crackdown During the hearing, advocate Syed Mohammad Haider Rizvi, representing traders selling kites and traditional manjha, told the court that safe and traditional kite materials were also being seized during drives against Chinese manjha. He alleged that traders were being harassed in the name of enforcement action. The High Court directed the government to ensure that action is taken only against illegal and dangerous manjha and that legitimate businesses are not targeted. Pollution Control Board asked to explain role The court also sought a response from the Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board regarding its role in the matter. The board has been directed to file an affidavit explaining what steps it is taking to address the issue. Court suggests identifying ‘hotspot areas’ The High Court observed that every city has certain areas where kite flying is more common. It suggested that such hotspot areas should be identified and placed under special surveillance to curb the sale and use of illegal manjha effectively. Senior officials ordered to appear on July 13 The next hearing in the case will take place on July 13, 2026. Senior officials from the Home Department, State Tax Department, Environment Department and the DGP’s office have been directed to appear before the court through video conferencing and submit details of the action taken so far.

stories.title: Detergent used to make fake milk in UP:20 litres increased to 80 within minutes, camera expose uncovers shocking racket
stories.summary: Milk is often considered a rich source of calcium and an essential part of a balanced diet that supports overall well-being and boosts metabolism. But what if the milk you consume turns out to be synthetic and potentially harmful to your health? Shockingly, several factories manufacturing fake milk have mushroomed across areas of Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan bordering Uttar Pradesh, driven by these huge profits and are involved in a large-scale synthetic milk racket. To expose the network, a Dainik Bhaskar reporter posed as a milk trader and infiltrated these illegal manufacturing units. The process of making synthetic milk is alarmingly simple. Soy oil and detergent paste are mixed together by hand before being blended into nearly 60 litres of water. To this, operators add 20 litres of pure milk along with around 2 kg of molasses powder or glucose. Skimmed milk powder is then added to thicken the mixture — producing nearly 80 litres of synthetic milk within minutes. The fake milk reportedly costs around Rs 25 per litre to manufacture, while the racket earns profits of Rs 25-30 per litre. In recent weeks, authorities seized 1,400 litres of synthetic milk in Bulandshahr and another 450 litres in Agra, pointing to the scale of the illegal trade. Read the full investigation Reporter reaches illegal factory in Rajasthan Using sources in Bulandshahr and Agra, the reporter travelled to Basai Nawab town in Rajasthan’s Dholpur district, where labourers were openly preparing synthetic milk. Workers there said they earn salaries of Rs 15,000-20,000 per month and can manufacture 80-100 litres of synthetic milk every hour. A labourer identified as Kedar Singh explained the process. “Urea and glucose are both used” Inside the ‘difference milk’ codeword During the investigation, the reporter discovered a codeword used in the milk trade — “Difference”. Fake or synthetic milk is commonly referred to as “difference milk”. The racket categorises adulterated milk into four levels: 2 difference 3 difference 4 difference Above 4 difference “We can supply any quantity”: Trader offers takers of fake milk The reporter later contacted a trader named Umesh after obtaining his number from a factory guard in Basai Nawab. “No problem, we can supply as much as you want” Another trader promises 50,000 litres daily Umesh later directed the reporter to Maniya town, nearly 40 km away on the Gwalior highway. There, another trader named Sonu negotiated a deal for fake milk supply. “No one catches us” “Shift your stock here, I’ll arrange 50,000 litres daily” The reporter told Sonu that the milk stock was stored near Tedhi Bagiya area in Agra. Sonu then suggested moving operations closer to Rajasthan. How fake milk passes standard tests Milk quality is commonly checked through two parameters: Normal milk typically contains: Synthetic milk manufacturers reportedly add molasses powder to artificially increase fat readings during testing. Glucose powder raises SNF levels to nearly 8%, allowing fake milk to appear genuine during routine checks. Fake milk trade worth ₹135 crore daily Uttar Pradesh consumes nearly 8 crore litres of loose milk daily. About 50% — nearly 4 crore litres — comes from western UP. According to a report by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), nearly 67% of milk products in India are adulterated. Applying that estimate to western UP suggests that around 2.7 crore litres of milk supplied daily could potentially be fake or adulterated. Milk manufactured at Rs 30 per litre is allegedly sold in UP at around Rs 50 per litre, creating an estimated daily illegal market worth Rs 135 crore Doctors warn of cancer and organ damage According to Dr Arun Srivastava, Chief Medical Officer of Agra Border areas become hub of fake milk industry Synthetic milk is reportedly being manufactured openly in homes and factories across: Authorities reportedly struggle to crack down due to the tri-state border network. Most fake milk from these regions is supplied to Agra, Aligarh, Mathura, Hapur, Bulandshahr, Meerut and Noida before reaching Delhi-NCR markets. The report alleges that enforcement agencies often fail to act effectively, with traders allegedly receiving advance information before raids. While official seizures in UP crossed only 5,000 litres in a month, traders caught on camera claimed they could supply 50,000 litres of synthetic milk every day. 40% milk samples failed in UP Between April 2025 and February 2026, authorities collected 39,568 milk samples across Uttar Pradesh. Out of these, 15,361 samples failed quality tests — meaning nearly 40% were found to be adulterated or fake. Despite the alarming figures, the report claims strict action from authorities has remained limited.

stories.title: Bakrid holiday shifted to May 28 in UP:Yogi government changes date; Maulana urges people not to offer namaz on roads
stories.summary: In Uttar Pradesh, the public holiday for Eid-ul-Adha, popularly known as Bakrid, has been shifted from May 27 to May 28. The Yogi government issued revised orders on Tuesday, stating that all government offices and banks will remain open on May 27 and closed on May 28 instead. According to the updated notification issued by Chief Secretary of General Administration SVS Ranga Rao, the decision was taken in view of the moon sighting and the revised date of the festival. Meanwhile, Muslim religious leaders have appealed to people not to offer namaz on roads to ensure that traffic movement is not disrupted. They also urged citizens to maintain cleanliness during Bakrid and follow guidelines while performing animal sacrifice. Religious leaders advised that sacrifices should be carried out only at designated places and that animal remains should not be disposed of in the open. Shahi Mufti of Aligarh, Maulana Ibrahim Hussain, said people should celebrate the festival peacefully while fully cooperating with the administration. Permission to pray on the road should not be given not only on Eid but on other days as well. Islam does not teach us to cause trouble to anyone. Roads are public. Everyone has a share in them. Shia religious leader says- We should not even look at cows with raised eyes Shia religious leader Maulana Saif Abbas said, on Bakrid you should perform sacrifice. In our country's constitution, only those animals whose sacrifice is permitted should be sacrificed. We should not even look at cows with raised eyes because our Hindu brothers worship them. He warned that if any person sacrifices a cow, they will be working against Islam. Islam says that other religions should be respected. There is no need to sacrifice cows. Before Bakrid, Yogi had said- Will not allow namaz on roads A week ago, CM Yogi gave a strict warning regarding namaz on roads. He had said that namaz will not be allowed on roads. If they agree with love, fine, if they don't agree, then another method will be adopted. Yogi said, If you want to read namaz, read it at a designated place. If the numbers are more, read it in shifts. We will not stop namaz, but we will not allow anarchy on the roads. Roads are not for reading namaz or gathering crowds of any kind. He said- People ask me whether namaz happens on roads in UP? I say- absolutely not. Roads are for common people to walk on. No one has the right to come and disturb traffic. Yogi further said, "Those people told me that sir, how will it happen, our numbers are more. We said- if you don't have space to live in your house, then control the population. If you don't have the capacity, then why is the population being increased unnecessarily? Everyone will have to live within the system. Everyone will have to accept the rule of law." Raised issue of namaz on roads during election campaign in Bengal CM Yogi had raised the issue of namaz on roads during the recently concluded West Bengal Assembly election campaign. Accusing former Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee of politics of appeasement, he had said that Didi makes people read namaz on roads. She imposes restrictions on Hindu festivals. In UP, no one can read namaz on roads. Roads are for traffic, not for namaz. No curfew, no riots, everything is fine in UP. Yogi government had imposed ban on reading namaz on roads The Yogi government completely banned namaz on roads in 2022-23. Orders were issued that namaz would not be offered on roads on Eid, Alvida Jumma or any other day. Religious events should only take place inside Eidgahs, mosques or designated religious places.

The way people sitting in the government are using their power is visible. Those conducting fake encounters are not the government, they are criminals. If any encounter has ulterior motives behind it, then understand that it is fake. Akhilesh said, policemen involved in fake encounters should definitely think about how the government is using them for its own benefit. It is turning them from officers into criminals. Policemen involved in fake encounters know that they are doing illegal work. Many police personnel conducting such fake encounters even become mentally ill. They kill others in a moment and themselves die bit by bit. The SP chief raised the issue of the 2021 Jaunpur Pujari Yadav encounter and said, when police get caught in fake encounters, the BJP government turns its face away from them. When policemen go to jail, their family members become victims of social humiliation. Where the public conducts their social encounter. BJP spokesperson Rakesh Tripathi has hit back at Akhilesh Yadav. He said, What is Akhilesh's relationship with criminals? The injury is to the criminal, but the pain is felt by Akhilesh. After every encounter, the pain of criminals is expressed through Akhilesh Yadav's tongue. The elimination of crime and criminals is necessary for society.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Bus accident on Lucknow-Agra Expressway kills 7; Australia raises Hormuz concerns at Quad meet in Delhi more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top headlines: 1. Australia raises Hormuz concerns at Quad meet in Delhi The Quad foreign ministers’ meeting concluded in New Delhi, with Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong expressing concern over tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and their impact on global oil and energy supplies. 2. Seven killed as bus overturns on Lucknow-Agra Expressway Seven people, including a Bihar Police sub-inspector and a prisoner in custody, were killed after a double-decker AC bus overturned on the Lucknow-Agra Expressway in Uttar Pradesh’s Unnao early Tuesday morning. The Delhi-to-Bihar bus carrying 36 passengers reportedly crashed into a divider near Auras police station after the driver allegedly fell asleep at the wheel. The vehicle overturned and several passengers were thrown out onto the road. 3. UP fuel smuggled into Nepal, border districts face shortage Petrol pumps across seven UP districts bordering Nepal are running dry as fuel allegedly bought at ₹100 per litre in India is being smuggled into Nepal and sold for nearly ₹135. Long queues, supply disruptions and illegal cross-border transport have triggered a fuel crisis in the region. 4. After petrol and diesel, CNG dearer by ₹2 Amid the Iran war, the price of compressed natural gas (CNG) has risen for the fourth time in the last two weeks. Indraprastha Gas Limited (IGL) increased CNG prices by ₹2 per kilogram on Tuesday, May 26. 5. CM Yogi targets SP rule; recalls people drying clothes on electric wires Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said that during the Samajwadi Party government, people used to dry clothes on electricity wires as power supply remained erratic, with electricity available at odd hours. He said the same people are now trying to make a political issue over the power cuts during the global energy crisis. 6. BJP bets on 57,000 Gram Pradhans ahead of UP polls In a first for Uttar Pradesh, the Yogi Adityanath government has handed administrative powers of Gram Panchayats to village heads instead of bureaucrats ahead of Assembly elections. The move aims to speed up rural development work, reduce pressure on officials and strengthen BJP’s grassroots booth network across 57,000 villages. 7. Iran claims downing of US MQ-9 drone over Hormuz Iran has claimed it shot down a US MQ-9B drone and opened fire at a fighter jet that entered Iranian airspace. According to a report by Al Jazeera, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said its forces targeted an RQ-4 drone and an intruding F-35 fighter aircraft. 8. Four killed as Innova crashes into trailer on Barabanki highway Four friends travelling to Kainchi Dham were killed and three others critically injured after their speeding Innova rammed into a trailer on the Lucknow-Sultanpur Highway in Uttar Pradesh’s Barabanki early Tuesday. Police suspect the driver fell asleep before the SUV crashed into the vehicle from behind. 9. Rape accused's throat slit in Gorakhpur: Body packed in a sack thrown into river In Gorakhpur, a young man was murdered, and his body was stuffed into a sack and thrown into the Ami River. The next morning, seeing the sack floating, people informed the police. With the help of local people, the police pulled out the sack and opened it, finding the body of a young man. There were deep wounds on his neck. His hands were tied. With the help of a sticker on his clothes, the young man was identified as Aditya Sahni of Sahjanwa. The police informed his family. 10. Ranveer Singh banned by FWICE over ‘Don 3’ exit Ranveer Singh has landed in controversy after dropping out of Farhan Akhtar's film Don 3. Following Farhan Akhtar's complaint, FWICE (Film Federation of Western Cine Employees) banned the actor on Monday. He will not be able to do any film until the Don 3 controversy is resolved.

stories.title: SSC exam chaos in Prayagraj:Students vandalize centre, block highway over server failure; new exam date to be announced soon
stories.summary: During the SSC-GD recruitment examination held in Prayagraj on Tuesday, candidates created a ruckus when the server failed. The examination was scheduled to be held in three shifts (First: 10 to 11 AM, Second: 1 to 2 PM, and Third: 4:30 to 5:30 PM) at Sunita Singh Sita Singh College, located in Andawa. The first shift examination started at the scheduled time of 10 AM. There were 600 candidates for this, but only 450 candidates were present. As soon as the examination began, the computer server went down. At this, the candidates started creating a ruckus. They started breaking the computers and chairs kept in the rooms. They started shouting slogans. After this, at around 11:35 AM, students also blocked the Prayagraj-Varanasi Highway. Police, who arrived at the scene, managed to calm the situation with great difficulty after half an hour. Following the commotion, today's examination was cancelled. The incident falls under the Sarai Inayat police station area. See 2 pictures of the commotion Sanjay Gupta, the in-charge inspector of Sarai Inayat Police Station, stated- It has come to light that several computers and classroom furniture have been damaged. The police have started investigating the incident. Legal action will be taken after identifying the students who indulged in vandalism. Additionally, steps are being taken to call a technical team to investigate the server-related issue and to reschedule the examination. SSC Regional Head Ashish Kumar Srivastava said - The loss caused due to technical glitch in the examination will be assessed and a report will be sent to the education department and the concerned examination authority. Candidates should also maintain peace. Also, today's exam has been cancelled. The new date for the exam will be announced soon. Meanwhile, local villagers and traffic police said - Vehicle drivers faced problems due to the jam. But, traffic was restored soon. Students had also created a ruckus on May 25 On Monday, a similar incident of vandalism occurred at the I-Tech Zone examination center of Sunita Singh Sita Singh Women's College in Prayagraj. In the second shift (1 PM to 2 PM), candidates created a ruckus when twice the number of examinees allocated to the center arrived. During this, hundreds of computer systems, monitors, ACs, coolers, CCTVs, servers, jammers, and water coolers, along with other equipment in several rooms, were broken. After this, they went to GT Road and blocked the traffic. Traffic remained halted for about an hour. Police forces who arrived at the scene brought the situation under control and pacified the protesters. During this, the police also took a student into custody who was fleeing with a laptop. Responsibility of examination center to Bengaluru firm SSC Central Region had entrusted the responsibility of conducting the examination to Bengaluru-based Eduquity Career Technologies Private Limited. The center management informed that a total of 650 computer systems were available at the I-Tech Zone Center in Andawa. However, in the second shift, 1035 examinees instead of 505, and in the third shift, 1034 examinees instead of 495, were allotted the same center. The center received allocation information via e-mail only on Monday. This led to a breakdown in arrangements. Exams Cancelled at 5 Centers Including Prayagraj Citing technical reasons, SSC Central Region had cancelled the second and third shift exams on Monday at some centers in Prayagraj, Kanpur, Lucknow, Gorakhpur, and Muzaffarnagar. The commission stated that all affected candidates will have their exams re-conducted. New admit cards will also be issued on the website soon. The list of canceled examinations includes SMT Ramkali Iqbal Bahadur Online Center in Kanpur, City Modern Academy in Lucknow, Maharshi IT Institute Online Examination Center in Gorakhpur, and Adarsh Pariksha Kendra in Muzaffarnagar, in addition to Prayagraj.

stories.title: Storm in UP, roof tanks blown away:Trees uprooted, 6 dead; heatwave alert in 39 districts
stories.summary: Today is the second day of Nautapa in UP. Early Tuesday morning, a storm hit Lakhimpur Kheri. Trees and poles were uprooted. Roof tanks of houses were blown away. Most districts remained cloudy in the morning. The sun kept appearing intermittently. As the day progressed, the heat increased. Hot winds gained momentum. Today there is a heatwave alert in 39 cities. Among these, 3 cities - Banda, Chitrakoot and Prayagraj - are on red alert. This means very hot winds will blow here. Before this, late Monday night the weather suddenly changed. A storm with a speed of 90 hit Lucknow. Such strong storms also hit Basti, Gorakhpur and Gonda that thousands of trees and poles were uprooted. In Gonda, Lakhimpur, Basti, Shahjahanpur and Sitapur, 6 people including children died in accidents related to storm and rain. Heavy rain accompanied by strong winds also occurred in Badaun, Ayodhya, Unnao, and Sambhal. The Meteorological Department informed - A major change in weather will be seen from May 28. There will be storms, dust storms and cloudy skies. There will be good rainfall across the entire state for 2-3 days. The temperature will drop by 8C-10C. Talking about the last 24 hours, Banda once again remained the hottest city in the country. The maximum temperature was recorded at 47.6C. In Maharashtra's Brahmapuri, the mercury stood at 47.6C. In Jhansi, the mercury reached 46C. Temperature was recorded at 45.8C in Jalaun, 45.5C in Agra, and 45.4C in Prayagraj. See pictures- How is there rain between no disturbance and Nautapa? Meteorologists say that the temperature in UP has been very high for the past few days. Due to intense heat, a large difference has developed between the ground and upper air temperatures. Apart from this, a trough line (an imaginary line creating a low-pressure area) is active from eastern UP to Chhattisgarh. A cyclonic wind zone has formed over south Bihar. A weather system is also active over Jammu-Kashmir and its surrounding areas. Due to this, the weather in UP has changed. Favorable conditions have developed for storms and rain. Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh informed- A new western disturbance will become active on May 28. Cyclonic wind conditions persist at higher altitudes in south Bihar and surrounding areas. In such a situation, there may be storms, rain along with lightning on May 29 and 30 in the state. Wind speed can reach up to 50 km/hour. What will the weather be like for the next 5 days?

stories.title: Rape accused's throat slit in Gorakhpur:Body packed in a sack thrown into river; deceased identified by clothes
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, a young man was murdered, and his body was stuffed into a sack and thrown into the Ami River. The next morning, seeing the sack floating, people informed the police. With the help of local people, the police pulled out the sack and opened it, finding the body of a young man. There were deep wounds on his neck. His hands were tied. With the help of a sticker on his clothes, the young man was identified as Aditya Sahni of Sahjanwa. The police informed his family. During the investigation, it was revealed that a young woman had filed a report against Aditya for molestation on May 21. Five years ago, she had filed a rape report against him and sent him to jail. That young woman got married only last month. These days she is at her maternal home. Aditya's maternal grandparents' home is also in her maternal village. Angered by the molestation report, Aditya had stormed her house and created a ruckus two days ago on Sunday. Enraged by the same incident, the girl's family members caught Aditya. They set his bike on fire. After that, Aditya did not return home. The next morning, his body was found in the river. The investigation revealed that enraged by him breaking into their house and assaulting them, the girl's family members slit his throat and murdered him. Then, they stuffed the body into a sack and threw it into the Ami River. This incident is from the Gida police station area. The police have registered a report against 23 people. Five have been taken into custody and are being interrogated. See 3 pictures Now know the full case in detail Closeness with girl grew at maternal grandparents' house, she accused him of rape Rajesh Sahni, a resident of Tikaria village in Sahjanwa police station area, works in paint-polish in Hyderabad. His son Aditya Sahni (26) lived in his maternal grandparents' village in a nearby village of Khajni. Due to the poor financial condition of the family, he also used to go to Hyderabad with them for work. He used to visit his maternal grandparents' house frequently, which led to him getting acquainted with a girl there. Initially, the families ignored it, but later the dispute escalated. The two had been in a love relationship for a long time, but the family was not agreeable to their relationship. Due to this, there were arguments between both families many times. On June 1, 2021, the girl filed a case of rape against Aditya at Khajni police station. The young woman alleged that Aditya had forcibly made physical relations. Aditya was jailed in this case. Later, after getting bail, he came out of jail and went to Hyderabad with his father. He started working there with his father. Came to the village 10 days ago, the young woman was also at her maternal home Aditya had come to his village from Hyderabad just 10 days ago. The young woman who accused him of rape was married on April 20 last month. On May 17, she had come to her maternal home. Aditya was also present in the same village that day. On May 21, the same young woman again filed a case against Aditya at Khajni police station, accusing him of molestation. It is alleged that Aditya, angered by the registration of the case, attacked the girl's family with eight to ten companions on the night of Sunday, May 24. They broke into the house, assaulted the women, and destroyed household items including TV and fridge. Two women were seriously injured in the incident. When villagers arrived hearing the noise, Aditya and his companions fled from there. Later, the girl's family members chased Aditya, caught him near Katghar intersection, and set his bike on fire. After this, they beat Aditya and took him away with them. As soon as this information was received, the police became active. Body found in a sack in the river under the bridge, identified by clothes Police continued to raid throughout Sunday night, but Aditya could not be found. On the morning of May 25, Aditya's body was found wrapped in a sack under the Ami River bridge in Bharsand, Gida area. His hands and feet were tied, and deep marks of being slit with a sharp weapon were found on his throat. Aditya's shirt had a tailor's sticker, through which Aditya was easily identified. SP North Gyanendra Kumar said- On the complaint of Aditya's mother, Sanju Devi, a case has been registered at Khajni police station against 13 named and 10 unknown persons under serious sections including murder and rioting. Five people have been taken into custody and are being interrogated.
