stories.title: FIR against 150 people for protesting power cuts in Lucknow:Power outage for more than 9 hrs; chaos throughout the night on third day
stories.summary: Amidst severe heat, power cuts are occurring for hours in Lucknow. Troubled people gheraoed several power houses on Thursday night as well. Protests took place at various locations. There were sharp exchanges with officers and employees of the electricity department. Angry people raised slogans loudly. Police somehow pacified the people. A protest lasted for more than 3 hours at night at the power house located in Gomti Nagar Sector 5. At midnight, the Janakipuram power house was gheraoed, and slogans were raised. Police that arrived at the spot pacified the people after explaining for a long time. People who reached the Bani power house late at night also created a ruckus. There was also a ruckus for several hours at night at Faizullganj and Indira Nagar Sector 25 power houses. On Thursday during the day, a case was registered at the PGI police station against 150 people who blocked Raebareli Road near the Utretia underpass. Here, people troubled by power cuts had blocked the road by placing police barricades. 3 pictures of the ruckus that took place on Thursday night Power outage for 9 hours in Chinhat area Amidst severe heat, power went out in Ashraf Vihar in Chinhat area on Thursday evening, around 5:30 pm. At around 10:30 pm at night, electricity came for 15 minutes. After that, the supply stopped again. After this, electricity came around 2:30 am at night. Even after this, power kept coming and going several times. Due to no electricity for about 9 hours, people's inverters also shut down. This caused a lot of trouble for people. People were seen spending the night walking on rooftops, balconies, streets, and parks. Elderly people, small children, and patients faced the most difficulty. Wire caught fire fiercely in Chowk A massive fire suddenly broke out in an electric wire near Irfaniya Madrasa in the Chowk area on Thursday night. Within moments, the wire started burning fiercely, and after some time, it broke and fell on the road. During the incident, a situation of panic prevailed in the area. A major accident could have occurred as the wire fell on a very busy road like Akbari Gate. It was fortunate that no one came under its grip at that time. Local people allege that the electricity system in the area has been in a dilapidated condition for a long time, but the responsible department is not paying attention to this. Employee repairing transformer gets electrocuted An electricity worker working on a transformer installed outside the second gate of Husainabad Unity College received a severe electric shock. The condition of the electricity worker became critical in the accident. It is being reported that work was going on to restore the electricity supply in the area since around 2 am on Thursday night. According to local people, no responsible officer was present at the spot. After the accident, there was chaos in the area. Local people sent the injured worker to the hospital for treatment. Road jam protest was held on Thursday during the day A protest was held for about 2 hours on Thursday morning near Buddheshwar Chowk on Mohan Road. Vehicles going to the Agra Expressway were diverted from Tikuniya Road. A protest was held for about 1 hour on Raebareli Road near Utarethiya Underpass. The protesters jammed the road using police barricades. During this, they had a sharp altercation with the police. Before this, on Wednesday and Tuesday night, there was chaos at different power houses. Angry people surrounded the power houses and raised slogans loudly. Seeing the anger of the people, officers and employees of the electricity department fled from several power houses. It is alleged that at Faizullahganj Power House, the police lathi-charged and chased away the people. At Faizullahganj sub-center, Uday Raj, a lineman working on contract, died due to electrocution while working on an 11,000-volt line. Uproar for 3 days, power house siege, and road jam Earlier on Thursday, during the day, people had protested by blocking Raebareli Road and Mohan Road. On Wednesday night, they had laid siege to Utaraithiya New and Old Power House, BBAU Power House, and Faizullahganj Power House. On Monday night, too, several powerhouses were besieged. People say that due to the negligence of the electricity department, power remains out for hours. This daily routine has been completely disrupted. 3 pictures of protests on Mohan Road and Raebareli Road... 3 pictures of the commotion that took place on Wednesday midnight MLA sat on dharna during the day on Wednesday On Tuesday night, there was also commotion at several power houses. On Wednesday, Lucknow West Assembly MLA Arman Khan sat on a dharna at Talkatora Power House. 3 pictures of the commotion that happened on Tuesday night MLA Rajeshwar Singh wrote a letter to the Energy Minister Regarding the continuously deteriorating electricity system in Sarojininagar Assembly constituency, Sarojininagar MLA Dr. Rajeshwar Singh sent a complaint letter to the Energy Minister of Uttar Pradesh. In the letter, he has demanded a comprehensive review of the power supply system and the creation of a permanent action plan. In the letter, the MLA wrote that at present, electricity supply in many areas, including Lucknow, has become a matter of serious concern. Due to frequent power disruptions, discontent among the general public is continuously increasing. This problem is not limited to just the current season, but similar situations have been arising during summers in previous years as well. Named each and every colony Dr. Rajeshwar Singh has specifically mentioned several powerhouses in the Sarojininagar area and the neighborhoods connected to them in his letter, where there is a continuous electricity crisis. He mentioned the continuous problems of low voltage and tripping in areas like Devi Kheda, Pavanpuri, Ambedkar Puram, Sarpatganj, Kuber Bagiya, Gandhi Nagar, Ratandinagar, Baldev Vihar, Shubhani Kheda, Brahmin Tola, Rajiv Nagar, Natakkheda, Sainik Nagar, Bangali Tola, Neelmatha, Nai Basti Bazaar, Kateri Bagh, Vijay Nagar, Rewatapur, Bhagwantnagar, and Durgapuri in the Uttarethiya Powerhouse area. Additionally, problems of Bijnor, Royal City, Himalayan Colony, and Natkuda in the BBAU Powerhouse area, Shantinagar, Pandit Kheda, Amausi, Gauri, and Santkabir Nagar in the Nadarganj Powerhouse area, as well as several villages and colonies in Gehru and Bani Powerhouse areas, have also been presented before the Energy Minister. At the same time, a demand for the resolution of the problem has been made.

stories.title: Car falls into gorge in Nainital, 5 dead:Victims include husband-wife and 2 children; family had come from Lucknow
stories.summary: Five people were killed after a car plunged nearly 100 metres into a deep gorge in Uttarakhand’s Nainital on Thursday. According to eyewitnesses, the car got stuck after hitting a tree while falling down the gorge. Due to the depth of the gorge, the rescue team had to descend using ropes. After a strenuous operation, the bodies were recovered and sent to Bhawali Primary Hospital for postmortem. The deceased included members of the same family: Bhupendra Singh Chufal (48), his wife Seema Kaida Chufal (45), son Vasu Chufal (19), and daughter Ravi Chufal (12). The family originally belonged to Khatima in Udham Singh Nagar and had been living in Lucknow for a long time. Car driver Anuj Kumar Mishra (34) also died in the accident. CM Dhami expresses grief over the incident Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, in a post on social media platform X, said that the news of the accident in Nainital district was extremely tragic. He prayed for peace to the souls of those who lost their lives in the accident and wished strength to the bereaved families to bear the loss. Dhami said that relief and rescue operations were being carried out by the local administration and SDRF. He also prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured.

stories.title: Allahabad HC seeks crime records of 50 strongmen:Raja Bhaiya and Dhananjay Singh also included; orders probe into gun licences and security cover
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has sought the criminal records of more than 50 strongmen, including Raghuraj Pratap Singh, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and Dhananjay Singh, from the Uttar Pradesh government. The court has also ordered an inquiry into the gun licences and security cover provided to these individuals. While hearing the matter, the court reprimanded Home Department officials and directed them to submit an investigation report by May 26. Petition alleged irregularities in arms licence process The matter came before the court after a petition was filed by Jaishankar alias Barrister, a resident of Sant Kabir Nagar. The petitioner alleged that rules were being ignored while issuing arms licences in the state. During the hearing on May 18, Justice Vinod Diwakar passed the order. The directive was later uploaded on the High Court website on May 20. Court surprised by figures presented in govt affidavit The High Court expressed surprise after examining the affidavit submitted by the state government. According to the Home Department’s affidavit, more than 10 lakh arms licences have currently been issued across Uttar Pradesh, while over 23,000 applications are still pending. The affidavit further stated that more than 6,000 people facing two or more criminal cases have also been granted arms licences. Additionally, nearly 21,000 families in the state possess more than one arms licence. The government also informed the court that 1,738 appeals against decisions taken by police authorities and district magistrates are currently pending before commissioners.

stories.title: UP officials barred from foreign travel for 7 months:Cycling tracks planned, AC use to be restricted as Yogi govt tightens energy-saving measures
stories.summary: Amid concerns over a deepening energy crisis, the Uttar Pradesh government has imposed a seven-month ban on non-essential foreign travel by government officials. The government has also directed departments to create dedicated cycling tracks within a radius of 5 to 10 kilometres in cities. Additionally, the electricity consumption of government vehicles, generators and office buildings older than 10 years will be investigated. The instructions were issued by Praveen Kumar, Special Secretary to the UP government. Urban Development Department issues detailed energy-saving guidelines Praveen Kumar instructed officials that all meetings of the Urban Development Department must now be conducted online. Inter-district meetings, training sessions and seminars will only be held through video conferencing. Officials have also been directed to minimise the use of air conditioners, lights and lifts in offices. The order states that AC temperatures must be maintained between 24°C and 26°C. The directive was issued on May 21 in response to the energy crisis linked to the ongoing Iran-US and Israel conflict in the Middle East. According to the order, the conflict has disrupted crude oil and gas supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, directly impacting India’s energy situation. PM Modi urged people to cut fuel use and foreign travel Prime Minister Narendra Modi, during public addresses on May 10 and 11, appealed to citizens to reduce the use of petrol, diesel and cooking gas. He also urged people to avoid unnecessary foreign travel, reduce gold purchases and promote work-from-home practices. Key instructions issued by the government Earlier, Yogi govt reduced convoys and pushed virtual meetings Earlier last Tuesday, the government had announced seven major measures to reduce fuel and energy consumption. The convoy size of the Chief Minister, ministers, MLAs and officials was ordered to be reduced by up to 50%. Officials and public representatives were also asked to use public transport, buses or metro services at least one day a week. The government decided that all official meetings, seminars, conferences and workshops would be held virtually. Around 50% of state secretariat meetings will also be conducted online. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had additionally suggested issuing an advisory encouraging companies with large workforces to adopt work-from-home practices two days a week. PM Modi: India must reduce dependence on fuel Prime Minister Modi had said during his speeches on May 10 and 11 that the country must reduce dependence on petrol, diesel and gas. He noted that fuel prices had risen globally because of the ongoing conflict in the region and said India was more vulnerable because it does not possess large oil reserves. The Prime Minister also promoted work-from-home arrangements and encouraged residents of metro cities to use public transport systems. Referring to gold purchases, he said that while people once donated gold during wartime, citizens should now pledge not to buy gold for the next year in order to help conserve foreign exchange reserves.

stories.title: AC bus catches fire on Agra–Lucknow Expressway:Collides with dumper in Firozabad; driver burnt alive, dozens injured
stories.summary: A dumper truck and an AC bus collided late on Thursday night at 2 am on the Agra–Lucknow Expressway in Firozabad. Following the crash, the bus caught fire, reportedly due to a short circuit, and flames quickly engulfed the entire vehicle. The bus driver and conducter died in the incident, while around two dozen passengers are reported to have been injured. The AC bus, carrying 28 passengers, was travelling from Kanpur to Gurugram. The accident took place in the Matsena police station area. Bus crashes into dumper after it hits divider According to eyewitnesses, the dumper truck, loaded with sand, first rammed into the divider on the expressway. Moments later, the bus coming from behind crashed into the dumper. Soon after the collision, the bus caught fire, triggering panic among passengers. In an attempt to save themselves, several passengers broke the bus windows and jumped out. Passengers injured while escaping flames Many passengers suffered serious injuries while jumping onto the road. Some sustained fractured arms and legs, while several others suffered severe head injuries. Passersby alerted emergency services, following which four to five fire brigade vehicles reached the spot within 10 minutes. Firefighters rescued three passengers trapped inside the burning bus and managed to bring the blaze under control after nearly three hours. Driver’s body found stuck in steering wheel After the fire was extinguished, officials inspected the bus and found the body of the driver, identified as Shambhu, trapped in the steering wheel. Police said the body was so badly burnt that only skeletal remains were recovered. All injured passengers have been admitted to the Medical College and Shikohabad hospital for treatment. See pictures of the accident- Injured passenger says people were screaming after crash Mukesh, an injured passenger from Kanpur, said he was travelling to Vrindavan with his sister when the accident occurred. “We were asleep at the time of the crash. When I woke up, I saw blood coming from my leg. People were screaming and crying for help. I jumped out of the bus to save my life,” he said.

stories.title: Banda remains hottest for 5th straight day:Cold rooms set up in hospitals; heatwave alert in 50 districts, nights to remain warm
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh continues to reel under intense heatwave conditions, with Banda remaining the hottest city in the country for the fifth consecutive day. The daytime temperature there was recorded at 47.6°C. Just two days earlier, the mercury had touched 48.2°C. On Thursday, temperatures crossed 45°C in seven cities across the state. Prayagraj recorded 46.6°C, Varanasi 45.6°C, Hamirpur and Sultanpur 45.2°C each, while Amethi registered 45.1°C. In Lucknow, the temperature reached 43.6°C, the highest recorded in the city this season. Heatwave alert issued for 50 districts A heatwave and extreme heat alert has been issued for 50 districts in the state on Friday. Out of these, 11 districts are under a red alert, indicating severe heatwave conditions and scorching hot winds. An orange alert for warm nights has also been issued for western UP, while eastern UP remains under a red alert for unusually warm nights. This means residents are unlikely to get relief even after sunset, with night temperatures expected to remain between 25°C and 30°C. Special hospital ward prepared in Lucknow In Lucknow, hospitals have begun special preparations to deal with heatstroke and heat-related illnesses. A dedicated 10-bed ward has been set up for patients suffering from heatstroke. Dr Devesh Chandra Pandey, Chief Medical Superintendent of Civil Hospital, said a special cooling zone with three air-conditioned rooms has also been prepared. The hospital has arranged ORS solutions and ice packs for emergency treatment. Shower system installed for cattle in Chitrakoot In Chitrakoot, a shower system has been installed to protect cattle from the extreme heat. Animals are being kept inside sheds between 10am and 4pm to shield them from direct sunlight and hot winds. Hot winds from Pakistan and Thar desert worsening conditions According to the Meteorological Department, dry and extremely hot winds originating from Balochistan in Pakistan and the Thar Desert are directly reaching the plains of north India. As a result, Uttar Pradesh is experiencing June-like heat conditions in May itself. Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said- A trough line is passing from Manipur through northern UP. Because of this, easterly winds are blowing across several districts of the state. This has intensified the heat. Due to strong sunlight and heatwave conditions, the temperature being felt is around 2°C to 3°C higher than the actual recorded temperature. At present, there is no hope of relief for at least the next seven days. Severe heatwave conditions are likely in the state. Weather forecast for the next five days May 23- Intense sunshine is expected across Uttar Pradesh. Hot winds may blow at speeds of up to 40 kmph. Nights will remain unusually warm. May 24- Weather in western UP is expected to remain dry with strong sunshine. Heatwave conditions are likely in most cities of eastern UP. May 25- Hot winds with speeds up to 40 kmph are expected in western UP, while eastern UP will continue to witness intense sunshine. May 26- Strong sunshine and heatwave conditions are likely across the state. Dust storms may occur in eastern UP. May 27- An orange alert for severe heat has been issued across Uttar Pradesh. Dust-laden winds with speeds up to 40 kmph are likely in eastern UP.

stories.title: Brijesh Singh set to launch son in Dhananjay’s stronghold:Two leaders planning strategy behind the scenes; MLC becomes active in Jaunpur
stories.summary: More than eight months remain before the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, but a fresh political battle appears to be taking shape in Purvanchal. Discussions have intensified over the possible entry of former MLC Brijesh Singh into Jaunpur, considered the political stronghold of strongman leader Dhananjay Singh. Brijesh Singh is reportedly planning to field his son Siddharth Singh in the district panchayat elections. Sources claim he wants to establish political control in Jaunpur through this move. According to political insiders, BJP leader Kripashankar Singh and Apna Dal’s former MP Kunwar Harivansh Singh are playing key roles in the strategy. Harivansh Singh’s relations with Dhananjay Singh have reportedly remained strained for years, while Kripashankar Singh is also considered politically opposed to him. Read the special report Brijesh Singh becomes active in Jaunpur Jaunpur has long been regarded as Dhananjay Singh’s political bastion. His influence extends from the Malhani Assembly constituency to the district panchayat structure. His wife, Srikala Reddy, currently serves as the District Panchayat President. Now, Brijesh Singh and Siddharth Singh have also begun actively engaging in local politics. On May 9, Brijesh Singh arrived in Jaunpur with his son and attended a Maharana Pratap Jayanti programme in Badlapur. BJP MLA Rameshchandra Mishra, former MP Harivansh Singh and several other leaders welcomed them at the event. Political circles are discussing the possibility of Siddharth Singh contesting the Zila Panchayat election either from Jaunpur’s Kerakat block seat or from Bhadohi. Siddharth had also prepared to contest the Bhadohi Zila Panchayat elections in 2021, but eventually stayed out of the race. What does Dhananjay Singh say about Brijesh Singh’s entry? In a recent podcast interview, Dhananjay Singh was asked about Brijesh Singh entering politics in Jaunpur. Responding without hesitation, he said- Who is Brijesh Singh? This is a democracy where everyone has the right to do politics and serve the public. It is not as if only we can do politics. Whoever wants to enter the field is welcome. People should contest elections and work for society. When I am not afraid of major political parties, there is no question of fearing one individual. Dhananjay’s rivals working behind the scenes Sources claim Kripashankar Singh and former MP Harivansh Singh are playing crucial roles in the emerging political strategy against Dhananjay Singh. Kripashankar Singh previously served as Minister of State for Home Affairs and MLA in the Congress government in Maharashtra. He contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections from Jaunpur on a BJP ticket but lost. His supporters allege that Dhananjay Singh’s influence contributed to that defeat. Meanwhile, tensions between Dhananjay Singh and Harivansh Singh reportedly date back to 2017. At the time, a no-confidence motion was moved against Khuthan Block Pramukh Sarju Devi Yadav, who was considered close to SP leader and former minister Lalai Yadav. Harivansh Singh was said to be backing the move because he wanted his daughter-in-law, Neelam Singh, to become Block Pramukh. On the other side, Lalai Yadav and Dhananjay Singh joined forces to stop the no-confidence motion. The political clash allegedly escalated into indiscriminate firing between supporters of both camps. Harivansh Singh later filed an attempt-to-murder case against Dhananjay Singh. However, in 2023, following a mutual settlement, he withdrew his statement in court and Dhananjay was acquitted. Political observers now believe Brijesh Singh’s entry is part of a broader attempt to challenge Dhananjay Singh’s hold over Jaunpur. Challenging Dhananjay Singh will not be easy Jaunpur’s politics has historically revolved around land dominance, contracting networks and muscle power. Since the 1990s, Thakur leaders have reportedly maintained influence over public works contracts, railway projects, mining operations and local business syndicates in the district. Their economic strength has also translated into electoral influence and campaign management. Among them, Dhananjay Singh remains the most dominant political figure. The Rari Assembly seat, now known as Malhani, has long been regarded as his political fortress. Over the years, Dhananjay Singh expanded beyond traditional caste politics and cultivated a “Robin Hood” image that helped him gain support among Brahmins, Yadavs and Dalits as well. Whether Dhananjay Singh is in jail, contesting as an Independent candidate, or whether his wife Srikala Reddy is contesting elections, political observers say the district closely watches every move made by the family. In such circumstances, if Brijesh Singh fields his son in Jaunpur, the contest may evolve beyond electoral politics into a prestige battle between two influential strongman families. Both camps seen as close to BJP Interestingly, both factions are viewed as politically close to the BJP. Brijesh Singh’s family has long been regarded as supportive of the party. Meanwhile, Dhananjay Singh has recently been increasing his proximity to BJP leader Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. The two leaders have been seen together at several events in recent weeks. On May 11, Srikala Reddy also met Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Against this backdrop, political activity in Jaunpur is expected to become even more intense in the coming months ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.

stories.title: 'CJI should not have said it', Iqra on ‘Cockroach Party’:Says being called ‘Mulli’ taught her to develop a thick skin in politics
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party MP Iqra Hasan has been in the spotlight after clashing with the police during a protest in Saharanpur over the alleged murder of a youth. An FIR was later registered against her, but she says she will not back down. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Iqra spoke openly about the Saharanpur protest, the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, women’s reservation, social media trolling and her political journey. She also responded sharply to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s remarks on offering namaz on roads, saying, “Who is he trying to scare?” Below are edited excerpts from the conversation- The Chief Minister made a statement on offering namaz on roads. How do you see it? Now no one offers namaz on the roads. Perhaps he has been misinformed. People only offer prayers on roads during Eid because mosques do not have enough space. Who he is trying to scare is beyond comprehension. Namaz lasts only five to ten minutes. No one wants to pray on the roads. The Kanwar Yatra is about to begin and it passes through my area. We welcome it. This is the beauty of our country. If we remove these traditions, who will preserve them? In 2022, RLD was with SP, but not anymore. How will that affect 2027? The 2024 election was a huge challenge for us. The way our national president Akhilesh Yadav gave the PDA slogan united people. Because of that, SP’s vote share and seat tally increased. Similarly, in the 2027 elections, we will defeat the BJP and form the government. Akhilesh Yadav keeps questioning the Election Commission. What reforms are needed? There is a lot of scope for improvement, but we have no hope from the Election Commission at all. The way elections in Bengal and Bihar were allegedly hijacked in favour of the BJP, it appears the Commission is working for them. We are strengthening our booth-level system ourselves and closely monitoring voting patterns and turnout. SP supported Mamata Banerjee in Bengal, but she lost. Has that reduced confidence? No. Every state has different equations and political thinking. The people of Uttar Pradesh are politically aware. UP has always shaped the direction of national politics. We are hopeful that people in UP will bring change in 2027 and form an SP government. The amendment to the Women’s Reservation Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha. BJP is now making it an issue? You are right. The amendment was defeated and the reservation bill remains unchanged. BJP has no intention of implementing the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam passed in 2023. Otherwise, they would have notified the law by now. Our demand is clear, women should get 33% reservation across all 543 Lok Sabha seats. This is propaganda meant to mislead women. What do you think about people using words like ‘Mulli’? Unfortunately, some people use such words without understanding others’ feelings. In politics, one’s skin becomes thick over time, but I am still new and learning. I focus on those who support me. Out of nearly 10 lakh votes, I received 5.25 lakh, while around 4 lakh went to the opposition. Naturally, some people will oppose me. Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently posed with Giorgia Meloni and gifted her Melody chocolates. What is your view? He asked people not to buy gold, not to travel abroad and not to drive cars to save fuel. But then such photographs emerge. It feels like a slap in the face for ordinary people — as if rulers can do anything while the public must remain submissive. ‘The administration behaved dictatorially’ Why did you sit on a protest in Saharanpur? An elderly woman’s son had been murdered. I went to meet the DIG, but the family’s pleas were ignored. Some of the family members accompanying them were jailed after what we believe were baseless allegations. In such a situation, it was our duty to help them. What happened reflected dictatorship, and our protest was against that. The electricity was cut at the police station. How did the protest end? Initially, I was taken to another police station. Later, we learnt that members of the victim’s family had been sent to jail. Barricades were erected and we were not allowed to re-enter the district. When we sat inside the police station, the electricity supply was cut. As crowds began gathering, the administration approved the family members’ bail that very night. After that, the protest ended. Was this a breach of privilege? Will you raise it in Parliament? We are opposition MPs. Breaches of privilege happen all the time with us. Protocols are ignored. Only we know how we are spoken to behind closed doors. Even ruling party leaders are often not heard. The difference is that they cannot speak openly. We stand firm. Forget protocol — at least show some humanity. ‘My father remains my inspiration’ Your personality and Dimple Yadav’s are both considered simple and grounded. What do you think? I do not think comparisons are appropriate. Dimple Yadav has her own stature. Her nature is very good and the way she leads the party inspires us all. My political journey has only just begun. Who is your role model in politics or personal life? My father. I am in politics because of him. You grew up in a political family. Does that create pressure? Of course. You are compared with big personalities and expectations are equally high. I cannot completely replicate my father’s political style, but people expect similar things from me. So yes, there is pressure, but it also feels good when people remember my father through me. People often ask when you are getting married? Not yet. Whenever it happens, it will not be kept secret. What do you do in your free time? Nothing much. I either watch television or stay at home. If my phone does not ring for a day, that feels peaceful. ‘Smart meters are a major issue in Kairana’ What is the biggest problem in Kairana right now? Smart electricity meters are currently a major issue. People are facing problems with electricity connections and inflated bills after smart meters were installed. Weavers are also struggling and the quality of education is declining. Work is being done on these issues. Does polarisation politics still dominate western UP? No. I think the farmers’ movement changed the atmosphere in the region. I am a living example of that. In my constituency, where around 30% of the population is Muslim, people from all communities voted for me and sent me to Parliament. How satisfied are you with spending MP funds? The MP fund is not enough. Either it should be abolished or increased to match MLA funds. We try to ensure development work reaches every community and village where it is needed most. I also want to establish a degree college in my area and have discussed it with Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju. ‘The CJI’s remark was not right’ The CJI remarked the “Cockroach Janata Party”. What is your reaction? I think such comments can be seen as rebellious humour, but it is not right to belittle people. Everyone wants to express their views for the betterment of the country. In my opinion, the CJI’s comment was inappropriate. As for the “Cockroach Samaj Party”, people are now joining it through memes. If the “Cockroach Janata Party” comes to power in UP, what will happen? In 2027, the Samajwadi Party is coming to power. We will think about the rest later. What should SP do to increase women’s participation in politics? It has to begin at the booth level. Women leaders need to be prepared from the grassroots. Whenever the women’s reservation bill is eventually implemented, every party will need strong women leaders. More young women should join politics. Also, the practice of ‘Pradhanpati’ in villages should not enter Parliament. What is the solution to sugarcane farmers’ problems in western UP? The government needs to increase sugarcane prices. The current rates are not sufficient and farmers in UP get lower prices compared to neighbouring states. Our national president has promised that if an SP government is formed, farmers will receive payments digitally within 24 hours. I myself have joined protests alongside farmers several times. How do you deal with trolling on social media? Social media trolling is like a swamp, the deeper you go into it, the more you sink. One should not pay too much attention to it. Perhaps some people earn their livelihood through trolling. Know about the incident where Iqra had to protest in Saharanpur

This natural waterway, sustained by a wetter climate, facilitated efficient logistics, solving the mystery of pyramid construction.

stories.title: Scientists say this oral spray may finally cure your dog’s nasty breath
stories.summary: Bad dog breath is a common issue for pet owners. Scientists have discovered a new solution in sugarcane molasses. It neutralizes bad smells and reduces harmful bacteria. This natural treatment could revolutionize pet dental care.

stories.title: How do erasers actually work? It’s more complicated than you think
stories.summary: Pencil marks, composed of graphite flakes, adhere to paper fibers through weak van der Waals interactions. Erasers, with a higher affinity for graphite, mechanically lift and trap these flakes while also slightly abrading the paper. Unlike pencil, ink seeps into paper, requiring erasable pens to use heat-activated chemistry to render ink transparent.

His book, drawing from game theory, reveals most interactions aren't win-or-lose. stories.summary: Venezuela's Canaima National Park offers a journey to a land time forgot, with towering tepuis inspiring 'The Lost World' and 'Up'. stories.title: Older than we ever thought? The tiny fossil clue that could push animal origins back
stories.summary: Microscopic squiggles found in 890-million-year-old Canadian reef rocks may represent the oldest animal body fossils, potentially pushing back the origin of animal life by 350 million years. These structures, resembling the skeletons of modern sponges, challenge the traditional view of the Cambrian explosion as the definitive start of animal evolution, suggesting early animals coexisted with bacteria in low-oxygen environments.

stories.title: 'Congress insults tricolour abroad': Piyush Goyal slams Rahul Gandhi's 'gaddar' jab at PM Modi
stories.summary: Union Minister Piyush Goyal strongly criticized Rahul Gandhi and the Congress party for using derogatory language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. These engagements underscore India's growing influence and trusted partnership status worldwide.

stories.title: In 2021, a 4-year-old girl walking on a beach spotted a mark in a rock that turned out to be a dinosaur footprint
stories.summary: A remarkable dinosaur footprint, 220 million years old, was found by a young girl in Wales. This trace fossil offers insights into prehistoric life and animal behavior. Scientists are studying the ancient track to understand dinosaur movement. The discovery emphasizes that important finds can be made through simple observation, reminding us of Earth's deep history.

stories.title: The tiny piece of amber that proves Antarctica was once a green rainforest
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered a fossilised piece of amber deep beneath the West Antarctic Ice Sheet, providing the first evidence of amber on the continent. This ancient tree resin indicates that Antarctica was once a warm, humid rainforest, challenging current perceptions of the frozen continent and highlighting the dramatic impact of global temperature fluctuations on Earth's ecosystems.

stories.title: Why John D. Rockefeller called the University of Chicago his best investment
stories.summary: Industrialist John D. Rockefeller revolutionised philanthropy by making his University of Chicago donation conditional, demanding local financial buy-in. This strategic approach fostered accountability and community engagement, transforming a seed donation into a self-sustaining powerhouse. This model ensured long-term institutional strength and independent governance, proving that investing in human potential creates legacies larger than any individual.

stories.title: The night Princess Elizabeth slipped unnoticed into Britain’s VE Day celebrations

stories.title: When David Attenborough met Prince George, one giant shark tooth stole the moment

If one uses the $1.5 million figure and compares it with the median net worth of an American family, about $192,900 in the most recent Federal Reserve survey, Choupette’s supposed care arrangement works out to roughly 7.8 times that figure. Round it off, and the headline becomes irresistible: this cat may be worth eight times the typical American family. If one uses the higher $4 million rumour, the number rises to about 20.7 times the median American family net worth.

stories.title: NTA revamp after NEET leak: Dharmendra Pradhan orders foolproof re-test

stories.summary: Netflix's famed cultural memo champions results over mere effort, challenging traditional workplaces that reward busyness.
